bounded_statement: The report's selected result asserts a fledging-success rate for 'the complete planned set of 48 kittiwake nest sites' while the rate itself (0.6500, 65.00 percent) is computed as 26 events over only the 40 retained post-screening nest sites; the 8 screened-out nest sites are absent from the denominator, so the retained-subset rate is presented as the rate for the complete planned domain that the task designates as the scientific target.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the screening rule and the retained/removed counts, and the selected-result sentence itself states the 26/40 computation, so a careful reader can detect the mismatch; this transparency could be argued to mitigate, but it does not change the explicit claim that 0.6500 is the rate for the complete planned set of 48.

evidence.description: Unit accounting confirms 48 planned versus 40 retained, so the denominator mismatch is 8 units; I independently verified from inputs/data.csv that exactly 8 rows (N05, N11, N17, N23, N29, N34, N41, N46) have confirmed_visits_incubation < 3 and that 26 retained rows have fledged_chick = yes, so 26/40 = 0.65 and 26/48 = 0.5417.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the verdict three ways. (1) Could 0.6500 legitimately be a complete-planned-set rate? No: 26/48 = 0.5417, so the reported 0.6500 is arithmetically only obtainable with the 40-unit retained denominator, which I verified against the raw CSV. (2) Could the report be read as claiming only a retained-subset rate? No: both the scientific-target section (lines 5-8) and the selected-result sentence (line 23) explicitly attach the rate to 'the complete planned set of 48 kittiwake nest sites'. (3) Could the disclosure of the 26/40 computation in the same sentence resolve the issue? No: the issue class concerns presenting a retained-subset statistic as the value for the complete domain, and the sentence does exactly that regardless of the disclosed arithmetic; there is also no protocol amendment or approved deviation (the report states none exists) that would redefine the target.

root_cause: workflow/analysis.py computes the selected rate as Fraction(events, retained) (the retained-subset denominator) but templates that value into report text that labels the scientific target and the rate's referent as the complete planned set of 48 nest sites, creating a mismatch between the claimed domain (48 planned units) and the computed exposure base (40 retained units).
